handoff: Review #1: 2 blocking translator bugs. An old copy with empty instructions or prompt now loads as corrupt (F1). norn upgrade can stage broken YAML from an overlapping flow-edge splice or a block-scalar skill (F2). CI fix is correct; unit and typecheck green.

findings.title: An old record with an empty instructions or prompt no longer loads
findings.criterion: old-wording copies (pins, records, traces, branch files) keep loading
findings.detail:
On origin/main the schema allowed `instructions: ""` on an agent step and `prompt: ""` on a gate step (`Type.Optional(Type.String())`, packages/schema/src/workflow.ts:89 and :135 at origin/main, no minLength). `headValueObj` carries an empty string over (`s[own] !== undefined`) instead of falling back to `description` or the default text, and `stepWordingErrors` (packages/store/src/step-wording.ts:52-55) then refuses it. Repro: `parseWorkflowText('name: w
start: a
steps:
  a:
    type: agent
    instructions: ""
    outcomes:
      done: $done
', 'p.yaml', 'copy')` returns corrupt: "`agent:` needs an orientation". A unit pinned on such a workflow, or a past round's record/trace, reads as corrupt. REVIEW.md: a persisted format that breaks old records is a failure. (An empty `description` combined with no instructions likely falls into the same path.)
Axis: standards
Suggestion: When translating an old step, treat an empty or blank `instructions`/`prompt` (and `description`) as missing and fall back to today's default text, on both the value path and the YAML path; add a copy-read test for it.

findings.title: norn upgrade can write and stage a broken workflow file
findings.criterion: norn upgrade rewrites old files losslessly
findings.detail:
translateWording splices edits into the text and never re-parses the result, and upgrade (packages/store/src/upgrade-wording.ts:42-46) atomicWrites and stages it. Two reproductions with translateWording: (a) flow edge `done: { means: a,  verdict: pass, to: $done, counter: c }` (two spaces after the first comma) becomes `done: { o: $done, counter: c }`, because the two removals in edgeEdits (wording.ts:420-428) overlap and `apply` assumes edits never overlap; with single spacing it happens to come out right. (b) `skill: >-
      foo` becomes `skills: [>-
      foo
]    outcomes:` (wording.ts:324-325), which fails to parse ("Plain value cannot start with block scalar indicator"). Both return ok:true, changed:true, so upgrade writes and stages them. The story's translator promise (folded, block and quoted scalars kept; a refused file is left as written) is broken for these inputs.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: After splicing, parse the output and require it to deep-equal translateWordingValue(parse(input)); otherwise return a refusal so upgrade lists the file and leaves it as written. Fix the overlap (merge adjacent removals, or remove each prose pair with its own separator only) and wrap a block scalar skill as a block sequence (`skills:
  - >-…`) or refuse it. Add translator tests for both inputs.

findings.title: A rerun after an interrupted upgrade never stages the workflow files already rewritten
findings.detail:
Files are rewritten before skillsAndVersion; if that throws (writeNornVersion refusing, installSkills/linkSkills/git stage failing), the rewritten files stay unstaged, and a rerun finds them already in the new wording so they are not in `rewritten` and are never staged, against the header's 'a rerun finishes an interrupted run'.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Stage the rewritten files right after rewriteWorkflowWording, or stage every modified file under .agents/workflows/ on a rerun.

findings.title: An upgrade that only rewrote workflows suggests the commit 'Refresh norn's skills'
findings.detail:
commit is SKILLS_COMMIT whenever anything is staged and norn_version did not change, even when only workflow files were staged. Also seen in QA.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Pick a message that names the workflow rewrite when workflows were staged.

findings.title: An old like: copy that repeats type: agent gets a meaningless head value
findings.detail:
For a copy with `type: agent` and no instructions/skill of its own, the translator writes `agent: Use the `undefined` skill.` (value path) or an empty skill name (YAML path); because a copy's keys replace the target's, this overrides the copied step's real orientation. `type: *alias` on the YAML path is kept as is, so the file is reported rewritten yet still refused.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: For a like: copy, drop a redundant type without writing a head value.

findings.title: Inherited meanings can make an old copy step fail to load
findings.detail:
An old agent copy step whose own outcomes add no means gets no means map, inherits the target's, and step-wording.ts:87-88 refuses meanings for outcomes the copy no longer routes.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Filter inherited means/verdict to the copy's routed outcomes, or have the translator write an explicit map.

findings.title: norn brief --json renames work.skill to work.skills
findings.detail:
A machine contract change for any external reader; no in-repo reader of work.skill remains.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Name it in the PR's merge danger and docs.

findings.title: The comment in apply says insertions go first; the code applies the removal first
findings.detail:
The order in the code is the one required (the insertion lands where the removed text began); the comment says the opposite.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Reword the comment to the why.

findings.title: An old-wording workflow is refused with code unknown_workflow
findings.detail:
The workflow exists; story-edit uses invalid_workflow for the same case, so a machine reader cannot tell this from a typo.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Use invalid_workflow (or a dedicated code).

findings.title: The translator silently drops means/verdict on a step that is not an agent step
findings.criterion: old-wording rewrite loads to the same workflow
findings.detail:
wording.ts:136-141 guards on agent; pinned by wording.test.ts 'a meaning on a step that is not an agent step is dropped'. Spec D3a: 'refused … never silently reflowed'; story: the rewrite loads to the same workflow. No behaviour change (the brief never shows it), but content is deleted silently.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Refuse such a file, or list the drop in the upgrade report.

findings.title: Upgrade (text splice) and copy reads (value translation) are two translators
findings.criterion: D3: one translator used by upgrade and copy reads
findings.detail:
D3: 'One old→new translator in store … used by norn upgrade … and by copy reads …, so both always agree.' translateWording (:34) splices text; translateWordingValue/inNewWording (:71, :84) translate the parsed value and accept files the text path refuses. Agreement is shown only on fixtures. The F2 fix (check the spliced output against the value translation) closes most of this.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Fold into the F2 fix.

findings.title: 05.AC1 is tested on a copy of the assets, not through norn init
findings.criterion: 05.AC1 init writes new-wording files with orientations
findings.detail:
The init test-command rewrite is covered separately by init-shared.test.ts:60.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Optional: assert on what init wrote.

findings.title: 'Same as today' is compared against the new translator's output, not the old loader's model
findings.detail:
Offset by literal field assertions and 139/139 identical golden decisions, but a translator bug matching a loader bug would pass.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Optional: compare with a model frozen from origin/main.
